topic: mean and median from a data list
problem:
The number of minutes each of 10 students spent on a homework assignment is listed below.
35, 48, 22, 60, 41, 35, 52, 29, 70, 38
By how many minutes does the mean of the data exceed the median of the data?

bad.why: Summing ten values, dividing by 10, sorting the list, and averaging the two middle values by hand is slow and error-prone when mean() and median() read both directly from the list.
Typed into Desmos, the same computation still needs the list sorted by hand to find the median; mean() and median() read both from the list.

algebraFirst.description: Adds the ten values (430) and divides by 10 for a mean of 43, sorts the list and averages the 5th and 6th values (38 and 41) for a median of 39.5, then subtracts.

explanationNotes: Make clear that with an even number of values the median is the average of the two middle values after sorting, which median() handles without sorting by hand; mean() is the total divided by the count. The answer is the mean 43 minus the median 39.5, which is 3.5.
notes: Verified: mean 43, median 39.5 (Python statistics and Desmos v1.11.4 both give 3.5 on the last gold row).
